cards.explanation: The answer is False. Paul writes, "Everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities…" (Romans 13:1). Everyone is a big word, friends. He doesn't stop at the believers in Rome. I like a word that doesn't leave anybody guessing.

The answer is that there is no authority except from God. Paul gives his reason right away: "…for there is no authority except that which is from God." Then he adds, "The authorities that exist have been appointed by God." He says why, friends, and he says it plain.

The word is judgment. Paul says whoever resists authority is opposing what God has set in place, "…and those who do so will bring judgment on themselves." Notice who does the bringing, friends. It's the one who resists. That's a lot like grabbing a hot pan with no mitt.
The answer is False. Paul says, "For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad." The terror is aimed at bad conduct, not good, friends. Good conduct can relax a little.

The answer is True. Paul asks, "Do you want to be unafraid of the one in authority?" Then he answers, "Then do what is right, and you will have his approval." He asks the question and gives the answer in the same breath, bakers. I wish my recipes were that short.
The answer is your good. Paul says, "For he is God’s servant for your good." Your good, friends. Paul puts you right there in the verse.
The word is sword. Paul says the one in authority "…does not carry the sword in vain." A sword is not for decoration, friends. That's a serious tool, and Paul wants the point to land.

The answer is as a matter of conscience. Paul writes, "Therefore it is necessary to submit to authority, not only to avoid punishment, but also as a matter of conscience." So there are two reasons, friends. One is about avoiding punishment, and the other is about your own conscience.

The answer is taxes. Paul says, "This is also why you pay taxes." He follows it with a reason: "For the authorities are God’s servants, who devote themselves to their work." Nobody loves the bill, friends, but the verse is clear.

The answer is False. Paul starts with "Pay everyone what you owe him…" and then lists four things. Taxes and revenue come first, then "…respect to whom respect is due, honor to whom honor is due." That's a bigger list than just taxes and revenue, friends.
